WHAT_THE_ABANDONED_CURSOR_WOULD_HAVE_COS.headline: ONE OF THIS REVIEW'S OWN THREE INCLUDED TRIALS IS ON PAGE 2 ONLY -- AND IT IS THE LARGEST.
WHAT_THE_ABANDONED_CURSOR_WOULD_HAVE_COS.why_this_matters_more_than_the_arithmeti: A screen run on page 1 would have reported a complete-looking cascade over 100 records, screened its remainder to zero, and been MISSING THE LARGEST TRIAL IN ITS OWN INCLUDED SET. Nothing in that page would have looked wrong: 100 records is a plausible surfaced set, the arithmetic would have reconciled with itself, and `k_unscreened_remainder: 0` would have been printed over a search that was 27 per cent short.
WHAT_THE_ABANDONED_CURSOR_WOULD_HAVE_COS.and_it_is_the_same_shape_as_the_phase_fi: `apixaban-vte` lost NCT02366871 -- one of its own two included trials -- to a `phase=[PHASE3,PHASE4]` filter, and that miss was RECORDED RATHER THAN REPLACED under P23. This is that class arriving through PAGINATION rather than through a filter term: a query parameter and an unexhausted cursor remove trials the same way, and only one of the two has ever had a guard.

the_P16_fourth_clause_meeting_its_own_ca: Every search this session recorded `returned == totalCount` with a null cursor as its pagination proof, and every one of those proofs was REAL AND UNTESTED -- the condition had never occurred, so the proof had never had an opportunity to fail. P16's fourth clause says a guard whose triggering condition has never arisen is unproven however green it reads. This is the first search in the session that could have failed that check, and it did.

scope_findings_from_the_COMPLETE_set._status: Recorded as observations on the complete surfaced set. NOT counts, NOT dispositions: no record here has been screened against any criteria and no arm roles have been read.
scope_findings_from_the_COMPLETE_set.the_condition_filter_reaches_well_beyond: The 137 include colchicine trials in Behcet's disease, IgA vasculitis, cutaneous vasculitis, multiple myeloma, oral ulcers, gout, pericarditis (CORP, CORP-2, ICAP, COPPS, COPPS-2), post-pericardiotomy syndrome, acute myocarditis, aortic stenosis, abdominal aortic aneurysm, chronic limb-threatening ischaemia, deep vein thrombosis, type 1 diabetes and COVID-19.
scope_findings_from_the_COMPLETE_set.and_the_split_question_is_now_askable_on: The object's three trials are of three different questions -- COLCOT randomises after MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION, CLEAR SYNERGY after MI within a 2x2 factorial alongside spironolactone, and CONVINCE after NON-CARDIOEMBOLIC STROKE. The complete set adds at least four more distinguishable questions: PERIOPERATIVE / POST-PROCEDURAL use (COP-AF n=3209, COPPS, COPPS-2, several post-ablation and post-cardiac-surgery trials), PERICARDITIS as a disease in its own right, PERIPHERAL ARTERY DISEASE (LEADER-PAD n=6150, and a limb-ischaemia trial), and INTRACEREBRAL HAEMORRHAGE (CoVasc-ICH, and an n=1125 phase 3). THIS IS A P21 DECISION ON A COMPLETE SET AND IT IS NOT MADE HERE -- it is now askable, which it was not this morning.
